title: Tenant-Scoped Salted Hash Mask Gate + Audit Trail for Observability Streams
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Trace and log streams currently surface fields that can contain customer-identifying data (user_ids, emails, session tokens) as freeform strings. This increases compliance burden and expands blast radius for engineers that query observability backends. Goal: introduce a deterministic, tenant-scoped masking gate that replaces sensitive contextual fields with salted hashes (non-reversible without controlled unmask flow), while supporting just-in-time unmasking for authorized incidents and preserving entropy for grouping and latency/error correlation across traces and metrics. The change should integrate into tracing hooks, metrics/log ingestion pipelines, and downstream dashboards, and must produce an immutable audit trail of all reveal requests.
impact: Reduces PII exposure in stored telemetry; enables safe querying/grouping across tenants; maintains ability to correlate latency/error events without exposing raw identifiers. Requires KMS usage per-tenant for salt/key derivation and small changes to query tooling for JIT unmask requests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingest pipeline replaces configured sensitive fields (user_email, user_id, session_id) with HMAC-SHA256(tenant_key, field_value || field_name) truncated to 128 bits by default
2) Deterministic salted hash enables stable group-by across events for a tenant while preventing cross-tenant correlation without tenant key

3) Unmask flow implemented: authorized operator can request a one-time reveal for a single event or trace via an approval workflow; the request generates an entry in an immutable audit ledger and requires HSM-wrapped key unseal
4) Dashboards (latency/error heatmaps, top-K slow traces) continue to support grouping by masked identifier and show a flag when data is masked
5) RBAC enforced: only roles with 'telemetry:reveal' permission can start unmask requests; all reveal operations are logged with operator, reason, TTL, and outcome
6) End-to-end tests covering ingest masking, stable grouping, reveal request/approval/unseal, and audit log creation
7) Performance regression <5% p99 ingest latency at baseline traffic profile, and unit-cost impact measured and documented
implementation_tasks: A. Tracing hook changes: add pre-emit hook to apply masking rules for spans and resource attributes
B. Log/metric pipeline transformer: implement masking operator in the ingest pipeline (Rust service) that reads tenant salt from KMS cache
C. Key derivation: design tenant_key derivation using KMS per-tenant envelope keys + HKDF; document rotation semantics
D. Unmask API + workflow: create service that accepts reveal requests, enforces RBAC + approval, performs HSM unseal, returns one-time plaintext (or redaction if denied), and writes audit row
E. Audit ledger: append-only store (Bigtable) schema and retention policy; integrate with Console for audit queries
F. Console UX: indicate masked fields in trace/trace-summary, add 'Request Reveal' flow with justification modal and TTL selector
G. Observability: add telemetry for masked-count, reveal-request-success/fail, KMS cache misses, and ingest latency delta
H. E2E tests and perf benchmark harness + rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> global)
I. Docs: runbook for operators, security whitepaper for compliance review
technical_notes: Mask algorithm: HMAC-SHA256(tenant_key, field_name || 0x00 || field_value) then base64-url encode truncated to 16 bytes. Truncation chosen to balance index size vs collision risk; collison analysis included in docs.

Tenant_key lifecycle: tenant_key is derived per-tenant from a master KMS wrap key using HKDF with tenant_id as info. Derivation reduces KMS calls and allows global KMS rotation without re-hashing stored tokens until reingestion is required.

JIT reveal: Reveals require HSM 'unseal' operation and produce a short-lived token reference; plaintext is not stored in long-term systems. Reveal operation writes an immutable audit entry with operator, justification, and TTL. Reveal responses are rate-limited and GPU/infra-intensive workflows are blocked by policy.

Sampling/tracing considerations: For sampled traces where full payloads are not retained, masked fields must remain consistent across sampled/unsampled copies to permit grouping. We will compute masked tag at instrumentation time when possible.
Backward compatibility: Provide opt-out header (redwood-observability-mask: none) for internal infra during migration. Default is mask-on-ingest for all external tenant traffic.
Performance: A thread-local cache for derived tenant_key and precomputed HMAC instances will minimize crypto overhead. Benchmarks expected to show <3% CPU cost increase for high-cardinality tenants.
Data retention: Masked telemetry inherits existing retention; audit ledger retention set to 7 years for compliance and is stored with restricted access and KMS encryption.
Edge cases: Non-string fields (JSON blobs) will be normalized to canonical form before hashing. Null/empty values preserved as special token 'MASK_NULL' to avoid collisions with actual hashed values.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete — implemented prototype HMAC masking in local ingest emulator. Verified deterministic grouping across 10k synthetic users.
2026-03-05: Security review kickoff with SecOps; concern raised about reveal audit retention and access scoping. Added audit ledger retention to 7 years and restricted access groups.
2026-03-08: KMS design reviewed; decided to use per-tenant derived keys with master wrap key to avoid per-tenant KMS objects. Liam to produce key-rotation playbook.
2026-03-11: Console UX mockups completed; PM accepted flows with minor wording changes. Frontend ticket created for reveal modal and justification capture.
2026-03-12: Began integration of masking operator into staging ingest pipeline behind feature flag 'masking-v2'. Initial perf tests show +1.9% ingest p99 latency.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hash collisions at truncation length could cause incorrect grouping. Mitigation: collision analysis, telemetry to detect unexpected join cardinality changes, and ability to increase truncation length per-tenant.
Risk: Unauthorized reveals due to RBAC misconfig. Mitigation: require two-step approval for top-tier reveals and ship RBAC tests in CI. Introduce 'canary reveal' role for limited scope trials.
Risk: KMS performance/availability impact. Mitigation: local KMS-derived key cache with TTL and graceful fallback to synchronous KMS call with retry. Monitor KMS cache miss rate.
Risk: Increased cardinality in downstream indices due to masked tokens. Mitigation: enforce hashed prefix bucketing and cap index cardinality via sampling + retention policies.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - internal: Enable masking-v2 for internal tenants only; validate grouping and dashboard UX (1 week)
Phase 1 - canary: Enable 10 external customers (opt-in) and run side-by-side comparison of masked vs raw (2 weeks)
Phase 2 - partial: 25% traffic across tenants with masking enabled by default; monitor ingest latency, KMS cache hit rate, and reveal request volume (2 weeks)
Phase 3 - global: Gradual 100% enablement with monitoring alarms and rollback flag (1 week)
Rollback: feature-flag off with fast-path for unmask queries to read raw payloads from hot-stage if available and replay if necessary
open_questions: Should we support reversible tokenization for a small set of extremely high-trust tenants, or keep only deterministic non-reversible masking?
What should be the exact truncation length for default masks (16 vs 20 bytes)? Run collision sims on production corpus to decide.
Retention for reveal audit rows: 7 years proposed — is this acceptable to legal, or do we need longer for certain geographies?
How will cross-tenant incident correlation (rare but valid) be handled when identifiers are tenant-scoped hashed?
